title: Rule out interleaving in six nonzero shared-hub calls
body:
## Summary

This scoped proof excludes interleaving in a six-call word on the shared-hub projector pool when each projector is used once at a nonzero exponent. Over any torsion-free abelian exponent group, a diagonal endpoint requires two consecutive triple blocks, in either order, with labels `S` and `T` constant within the respective blocks. The endpoint is `diag([S],[S],[S+T],[T],[T])`. Its targets use disjoint sets of paid labels, so total rational target rank is at most total paid rank.

The first nonzero augmentation degree of each triple supplies a common nonzero initial form. Their product lets the cross-commutator lemma force the block order even at five relations, when one triple can vanish in degree one. This answers the six-nonzero-call question in the [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718436).

Credit Ali Romman for the pool in [#7707](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7707) at `57e24923b609d2588b83321f530fa2a1e75ed364` and the cross-commutator lemma in [#7711](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7711) at `ac185e4529a01156f7b574555b50827f8cb645bb`. Credit Jerry Jiaheng Chen for the augmentation chronology method in [#6782](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6782).

## Evidence

The proof is in `research/shared-hub-single-pass/README.md`. The registered verifier multiplies all 527,040 full Laurent matrices across 720 orders and 732 signed label tuples at five relations. It found 792 diagonal endpoints and checked every diagonal entry against the formula. The direct command took 2.61 seconds locally. The registered replay and committed-byte, mode and source-history checks passed.

Run from the repository root with CPython 3.12.15 and the standard library.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/shared-hub-single-pass
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/shared-hub-single-pass --check-source-history --check-modes
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/shared-hub-single-pass/verify.py
```

The direct check prints `PASS_SHARED_HUB_SINGLE_PASS cases=527040 diagonal=792`.

## Scope and open obligations

The proof covers precisely six nonzero calls in the fixed original register coordinates. The finite replay uses an infinite cyclic exponent group. The written proof handles other torsion-free abelian groups. Repeated types, zero exponents and changed registers require separate arguments. Native realization, physical storage and restoration, and the complete recursive invoice remain open. Predecessor replays, the selected cold replay, Lean and Docker were unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Can a seven-call word with five relations interleave the triples with all calls nonzero and the repeated type separated by an opposite-triple call? Start with one repeated A type. Compare the sum of its initial forms in the private square with their separate contributions to the first mixed degree.

## Related open work

- [#7707](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7707) supplies the six-projector pool and studies its geometry.
- [#7711](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7711) treats arbitrary repetitions at four relations. Its larger-budget control uses zero calls.
- [#7710](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7710) studies a separate fresh-bridge alphabet and explicitly leaves out this six-projector pool.
